content: 1. The safety and efficacy of a 3% surgical procedure irrigation solution have not been established for children under 12 years of age. For individuals aged 12 years and older, the recommended dosage is 15 mL of a 70% solution or 10-20 mL every 2 hours orally until diarrhea occurs. 2. Sorbitol can reduce the systemic levels or effectiveness of lamivudine through mechanisms that are not fully understood. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. A pediatric study (ARROW trial) demonstrated that sorbitol-containing solutions decreased systemic exposure to lamivudine oral solution. This resulted in lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine exposure, and more frequent development of viral resistance compared to children receiving lamivudine tablets. 3. The combination of sodium polystyrene sulfonate and sorbitol has been implicated in cases of colonic necrosis. The exact mechanism is unknown, and it is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Sorbitol and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored closely when these drugs are used together. 5. The combination of dichlorphenamide and sorbitol can increase the toxicity of each other due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs can cause metabolic acidosis. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 6. Excessive bowel activity, diarrhea, edema, dehydration, fluid and electrolyte losses, hyperglycemia, lactic acidosis, dry mouth (xerostomia), vomiting, abdominal discomfort, nausea, and anuria (in cases of irrigation) are potential adverse effects. Acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or other symptoms of appendicitis or undiagnosed abdominal pain should be evaluated promptly. 7. Caution is advised in patients with severe cardiopulmonary or renal impairment, as large volumes of the solution may result in fluid overload and/or electrolyte imbalances. 8. Patients should consult a healthcare professional if they are taking mineral oil or have noticed a sudden change in bowel habits lasting over two weeks. If rectal bleeding or no bowel movement occurs after using this product, they should stop use and seek medical advice, as these could be signs of a serious condition. 9. In case of overdose, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. 10. Patients unable to metabolize sorbitol should use this product with caution. Sorbitol may cause hyperglycemia in patients with diabetes. 11. Pregnant women can generally use this product safely, as controlled studies have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 12. Sorbitol has poor absorption when administered orally or rectally. It is primarily metabolized in the liver to fructose. 13. Adding plans to a formulary comparison allows for evaluation of formulary status relative to other drugs in the same class. Formulary information may vary and is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider. 14.
